title: Sedge and the Firefly Watering Round
description: A little sage-green watering truck softens his mist for thirsty herb rows, leaves a dry path for glowing fireflies, then rests beside the old red barn.

Sedge.role: Main character; a little orchard watering truck
Sedge.color: Rounded sage-green cab and body with a buttercream water tank, narrow dark-green fenders, and one tiny cream droplet emblem on each door
Sedge.bodyShape: Small watering truck with four sturdy charcoal tires and a short silver misting bar mounted low behind the tank; no arms or hands
Sedge.face: Exactly two gentle dark-hazel eyes located in the two front headlights; no windshield eyes and nothing else resembling eyes; friendly grille smile
Sedge.accessories: Silver misting bar; small amber roof beacon that stays off during most scenes; no lettering, logos, or numbers

Lark.role: Supporting character; a small barn swallow
Lark.color: Warm-brown feathers with a pale cream chest
Lark.bodyShape: Small barn swallow with tiny wings; no clothes or accessories
Lark.face: Dark bead eyes and a gentle expression

settingBible.Herb Farm: A peaceful herb-and-flower farm bordered by an old red barn, with rows of lavender and other thirsty plants, a dry path between rows, and evening fireflies
settingBible.visualStyle: Warm polished 3D children's illustration, soft rounded farm vehicle and swallow, golden afternoon fading to moonlit night, one scene per page, and no readable text on story pages

continuityRules: Sedge keeps sage-green body, buttercream tank, dark-green fenders, cream droplet emblems, and eyes only in the two headlights.
Lark stays a small warm-brown barn swallow with cream chest and no clothing.
Keep plant watering and firefly wording general; avoid exact firefly counts such as dozens.
Pages 9–14 use soft firefly language that can fit loose art counts.
No rescue, danger, lettering, logos, or numerals in artwork.
Every illustration is one continuous scene with no panels, collage, grid, text, badge, logo, or readable words on story-page artwork.

pages.text: Sedge rolled past the old red barn as the warm afternoon began to cool.
pages.illustrationScene: Sage-green watering truck Sedge rolls slowly past an old red barn in warm late-afternoon light with farm rows beyond.
pages.continuityNotes: Sedge alone on page 1; Lark absent. Headlight eyes only.

pages.text: The young herb rows looked thirsty after a long sunny day.
pages.illustrationScene: Sedge looks toward slightly drooping young herb seedlings in neat rows after a warm day, with the red barn beyond.

pages.text: Sedge opened his gentle misting bar, but his first spray was much too wide.
pages.illustrationScene: Sedge tests his low silver misting bar with a gentle but too-wide fan of water over the edge of a row while Lark watches from a fence.
pages.continuityNotes: First spray too wide; plants remain safe. Soft details only.

pages.text: Soft and slow, chirped Lark from the fence. The tiny leaves only need a little.
pages.illustrationScene: Lark perches on a wooden fence near Sedge as if offering calm advice while watering is paused.

pages.text: Sedge turned the mist down until it floated as lightly as evening fog.
pages.illustrationScene: Sedge produces a much finer mist like evening fog over a short row of small herbs while Lark watches.

pages.text: The lavender leaves sparkled with tiny drops instead of bending under the water.
pages.illustrationScene: Close peaceful view of Sedge beside lavender plants sparkling with tiny droplets, stems upright, Lark nearby.
pages.continuityNotes: Gentle mist on lavender; soft wording.

pages.text: Next he misted the other thirsty rows, moving slowly from plant to plant.
pages.illustrationScene: Wider farm view of Sedge moving slowly past herb and berry rows with fine mist trailing gently behind.
pages.continuityNotes: Keep plant watering general rather than an exact crop-by-crop checklist.

pages.text: Sedge left a dry path between the rows for the nighttime visitors.
pages.illustrationScene: Sedge waters near the rows while leaving a clean dry path winding between the plants as sunset fades toward violet.
pages.continuityNotes: Dry path left for nighttime visitors; avoid exact path counts.

pages.text: As twilight turned violet, a soft firefly blinked beside the lavender.
pages.illustrationScene: A soft glowing firefly appears beside lavender as Sedge and Lark notice it under violet twilight.
pages.continuityNotes: Soft firefly wording; do not insist on exact firefly counts.

pages.text: Soon more and more gentle lights twinkled along the dry path Sedge had left.
pages.illustrationScene: Many soft golden fireflies drift along the dry path between watered herb rows while Sedge watches happily.
pages.continuityNotes: Use more-and-more wording instead of exact firefly counts like dozens.

pages.text: Lark swooped quietly overhead while Sedge watched the fireflies drift between the rows.
pages.illustrationScene: Lark glides gently above Sedge as fireflies float through the upper farm rows and barn windows begin to glow.
pages.continuityNotes: Soft firefly drift; no exact counts.

pages.text: The watered leaves smelled fresh, and the little plants stood calm and bright together.
pages.illustrationScene: Fresh upright leaves and flowers sparkle with tiny droplets beneath moonrise while Sedge looks over the peaceful garden.
pages.continuityNotes: Garden looks fresh and calm; soft general plant wording.

pages.text: Sedge closed his misting bar and parked beside the old barn.
pages.illustrationScene: Sedge rests parked beside the old red barn with misting quiet; Lark perched nearby under moonlit blue evening.

pages.text: The fireflies made a tiny glowing trail past his wheels and into the meadow.
pages.illustrationScene: A delicate trail of fireflies passes near Sedge's wheels and continues toward the meadow while he watches sleepily by the barn.
pages.continuityNotes: Soft glowing trail; no exact firefly counts.

pages.text: Sedge smiled beneath the moon and whispered goodnight to the little garden. Drink slowly and grow.
pages.illustrationScene: Sedge rests calmly beside the red barn under a bright moon while Lark perches nearby and soft firefly lights linger along the path.
pages.continuityNotes: Calm bedtime ending; soft garden goodnight.
